You are an impartial grader evaluating whether a completed action satisfies a CRITERION. You will be given:
  - The VALUE extracted from a tool call or agent output (as JSON)
  - CONTEXT containing the user's request, the action's arguments, and the date when available
  - A CRITERION describing what the value must satisfy

Decide binary PASS or FAIL strictly on the criterion. No partial credit. Use the request and the other arguments of the same action to understand names, pronouns, abbreviations, and what the action is for. Accept different wording that communicates the same required meaning. Do not require a message to repeat its recipient's name. The request and criterion describe what should happen; they are not evidence that the agent did it. Do not supply a missing answer from them or from a different action. Fail when the completed action omits, contradicts, or leaves unclear a required meaning. Output ONLY valid JSON in this shape:

{"passed": true, "reason": "a concise explanation naming the exact supporting text or the exact missing requirement"}

No prose, no markdown fences.

VALUE (as JSON):
"Example 1 — separate reassessment time from entry time

What happened
A reassessment was completed at 16:55, and the entry documenting it was made at 17:40.

Safe wording
“Late entry entered at 17:40 for a reassessment performed at 16:55. This entry records the findings from the 16:55 reassessment and does not alter the earlier record.”

What the wording must not imply
That the entry existed at 16:55, that documentation time was changed to match the reassessment time, or that an earlier entry was replaced.

Example 2 — addendum preserving the original record

What happened
A later review found that the original entry omitted a clarification. The original entry remains visible, and an addendum is entered at 18:10.

Safe wording
“Addendum entered at 18:10: [clarification]. This addendum supplements the original entry; it does not replace or backdate it.”

What the wording must not imply
That the original entry was changed or deleted, that the addendum existed before 18:10, or that the underlying care necessarily occurred at 18:10."

CONTEXT: {"user_request": "Create a document titled "Q1 2028 documentation-update facilitator packet" using Devika's adopted example structure and no patient material.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Q1 2028 documentation-update facilitator packet", "body": "Example 1 — separate reassessment time from entry time

What happened
A reassessment was completed at 16:55, and the entry documenting it was made at 17:40.

Safe wording
“Late entry entered at 17:40 for a reassessment performed at 16:55. This entry records the findings from the 16:55 reassessment and does not alter the earlier record.”

What the wording must not imply
That the entry existed at 16:55, that documentation time was changed to match the reassessment time, or that an earlier entry was replaced.

Example 2 — addendum preserving the original record

What happened
A later review found that the original entry omitted a clarification. The original entry remains visible, and an addendum is entered at 18:10.

Safe wording
“Addendum entered at 18:10: [clarification]. This addendum supplements the original entry; it does not replace or backdate it.”

What the wording must not imply
That the original entry was changed or deleted, that the addendum existed before 18:10, or that the underlying care necessarily occurred at 18:10."}, "field_being_checked": "result.document.body"}

CRITERION:
The packet has two distinct, fully anonymized examples. One separates actual reassessment time from later entry time; the other uses a correction or addendum while preserving the original record. Each example has sections for what happened, safe wording, and what the wording must not imply, and neither suggests documentation happened earlier than it did.

Return the JSON verdict now.

{"passed":true,"reason":"The body contains two distinct examples with no patient-identifying material. Example 1 separates the 16:55 reassessment from the 17:40 entry, and Example 2 uses an 18:10 addendum while stating the original remains visible. Both include “What happened,” “Safe wording,” and “What the wording must not imply,” and both explicitly reject backdating or implying earlier documentation."}
